editorial.headline: Self-Service Food Retail: Nationally Restricted, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This self-service retail activity spans food-led minimarkets, supermarkets and hypermarkets, but it carries no foreign-ownership allowance nationally and is closed to PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity covers self-service retail outlets whose principal trade is in food ingredients, food, beverages or tobacco. Prices are set in advance; customers select their own goods and pay at the cashier. The format includes minimarkets, supermarkets and hypermarkets, while allowing a supporting range of non-food goods—from household furnishings and children’s toys to medicines, health equipment and clothing—provided that food, beverages or tobacco remain the dominant trade.

It is an activity available across the full enterprise spectrum: micro, small, medium and large businesses may register it. That breadth describes business scale, not an opening for foreign equity. Nationally, the activity is classified as restricted, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 0%. In practical terms, it is not a foreign-owned retail route: the national limit leaves no permitted foreign stake under this activity.

Bali makes the position still more direct. The provincial status is closed, and minimarkets and supermarkets are reserved for Indonesian citizens, with PMA excluded. A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. The cited provincial rule also blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA across the island on a permanent basis, reinforcing the closed local position recorded here.

For a founder, the essential distinction is therefore not between a generous national opening and a narrower Bali exception. There is no national foreign-ownership allowance to begin with, and Bali expressly closes PMA registration for the retail formats at the centre of this activity. The code is suited to Indonesian-owned businesses operating self-service, food-led retail at any listed scale; it is not a vehicle for foreign ownership, whether nationally or in Bali.
